gaps: FAA primary reports not opened: DOT/FAA/AR-00/44 (Tomblin, Raju, Liew, Smith), AR-02/80, AR-02/121, AR-03/75, AR-99/49. DTIC (apps.dtic.mil) answered 'The request is blocked' to curl and 403 to WebFetch; tc.faa.gov and actlibrary.tc.faa.gov timed out; the Raju slide deck on amtas.washington.edu was opened but is a project overview with no damage-size data. FAA numbers appear here only as citations inside RMC theses (Clarke, Boctor, Pach), tagged secondary.

No primary FAA/Airbus/Boeing BVID definition document opened; the 0.25-0.5 mm (Boeing), 0.5 mm (NPL), 1.27-2.54 mm (NASA), 1.27 mm (0.05 in) values are secondary (Clarke, Boctor, Pach). The only primary BVID criterion read is NASA Langley's 0.05 in dent for composite-faced sandwich (McGowan and Ambur 1998).

Paywalled or unopened experimental aluminium-honeycomb impact papers: Foo, Chai and Seah (Compos Struct 2008), Crupi, Epasto and Guglielmino (2012, 2014), Akatay et al. (2015), Hazizan and Cantwell (2003), Zhou and Hill (2009), Zhou and Stronge, Olsson, Minakuchi, Shuaeib and Soden, Lacy and Hwang, Shipsha and Zenkert, Tariq et al. (2021). Foo numbers appear only through Pach's summary; Tariq and McQuigg only through Boctor.
RMC Wheeler thesis (2024, edge-distance CAI of metallic honeycomb) not opened (repository handle returned an HTML page, no PDF located). Benotto thesis (dent size vs stress) downloaded but not read.

Residual-strength fraction versus dent depth for aluminium faces on aluminium honeycomb: no source read gives an undamaged baseline next to a damaged value for the same aluminium-core panels (Pach prints only the singly-dented 66.9 kN peak and the 9 % second-dent effect; Gilioli has Nomex core with very scattered intact loads; Castanie has brass skins and one strength figure, 2 %).
No dent growth under compression versus load in numbers beyond Castanie's qualitative 'abrupt' growth; FAA propagation data (Tomblin, Shyprykevich) not accessible.

Beryllium: no through-thickness or short-transverse elongation for SR-200 sheet; no Charpy or instrumented-impact energy value (a DTIC cross-rolled sheet table and DTIC ADA021116 / AD0855716 were blocked; the search snippet's 8 % longitudinal and 14 % transverse elongation for 0.020-0.063 in sheet is NOT recorded); no K_IC for SR-200 sheet (only 1971 pressed and forged block, 10-11 ksi-in^1/2, and S-200 23 ksi-in^1/2 cited); no test of thin beryllium sheet under point impact, drop or puncture reporting dent versus crack; no beryllium mirror or panel micrometeoroid test report with damage mode found beyond the 1965 hypervelocity block/tube test (NASA TN D-3018). FZKA 6376 (S-200F irradiation database) was opened but the text layer lost the unit symbols and no room-temperature unirradiated K_IC was extracted.
SR-200 data sheet says 'hot rolling'; the brief's 'cross-rolled' is not on the sheet. Grain/texture, orientation and thickness of the 345 MPa and 10 % minima are not stated.

Hexcel: only the main HexWeb Attributes and Properties brochure (CR III 5056 row) was used; the CR III product data sheet and any Hexcel statement on crushed-core residual properties or core-to-skin peel behaviour were not read. AF 163-2U adhesive data not looked up (outside this brief).

Detection: no smallest detectable core-crush or disbond size for ultrasonic pulse-echo, through-transmission, thermography, shearography or laser profilometry on METAL faces. Tap-test PoD (Genest 2023, 0.5 mm Al skins) is the only quantified inspection limit. Seen only in search snippets and therefore not recorded: tap testing suitable for skins under 0.080 in (FAA-related handbook text), flash thermography 6 mm and 10 mm disbonds for 1 mm and 2 mm GFRP skins, Sofema's 10 mm tap threshold. Hsu's tap-test papers and Sandia/FAA AANC NDI validation reports not opened.

Dent relaxation of metal faces versus time: no quantified metal-face relaxation found. The 30 um per week (Prior) is a CFRP face; Castanie's springback is brass under quasi-static indentation; Minakuchi's 0.95 mm in 5 min is a foam-core sandwich (secondary).

Structural health monitoring of large structures (acoustic emission, strain-gauge arrays, pressure-decay monitoring): not found. Only Gilioli's one-sentence aim (sensor network can recognise impact occurrence, location and energy). NASA 20110014302 (honeycomb SHM modelling) was downloaded but not read.

Hail: Kim and Kedward (AIAA J 2000) and Kim, Welch and Kedward (Compos A 2003) are paywalled and unopened; UCSD 2010 and 2013 reports used instead. No hail test on aluminium-faced HONEYCOMB found open: Shi et al. 2025 (IJMS, polymer-core aluminium panels), Kim's ASC30 paper (Nomex core, 50.8 mm ice; dpi-proceedings returned 403), Penn State CFRP/Nomex hail paper, Anghileri's ice-on-aluminium work and the Wollongong steel-sheet thesis (dent depth ~ sqrt(E)/sqrt(t sigma_y) from a search snippet) were not opened. Hayduk NASA AIAA 72-335 (hail damage to aircraft surfaces) abstract only, no numbers. Marshall et al. test aluminium panels per its history section but report no aluminium results. Ice densities are not printed in any of the hail sources read; densities given in notes are derived and labelled so. Stacbond ACP velocities and energies are in image-only protocol pages.

The Kim 2010 Table 8 (FTE) arrives flattened by text extraction; the assignment of cells to ply count and sphere diameter is inferred (consistent with sphere density 0.87-0.92 g/cm3 and with the 2013 slide FTE = 489 J for 16 plies and 61 mm). Verify against the PDF figure before use.

Wang et al. 2017 Tables 1-3 are internally inconsistent with the paper's own text (dent depth versus wall thickness and cell side) and the drop-ball mass is not stated; treat their dent depths as indicative only.

Figure-only data not read: Clarke Figures 4-4, 4-5, 4-13, 4-18, 4-24; Pach force-displacement and dent profiles; Prior force histories; Castanie strength-vs-indentation figure; Gilioli Fig 9. No value was taken from any figure; all values are from text or tables.

Quotes are verbatim from the PDF text layer with whitespace collapsed, ligatures (fi, fl) expanded, and line-end hyphens at wrapped words closed up; superscripts (for example 1/2 after ksi-in) sit on separate lines in the text layer. Page numbers in 'location' are PDF page indices of the downloaded file, not printed folios (except Hexcel brochure p.13 and p.27, which coincide).
